title: Rock Pool
text: Tess and Grandad walked down to the beach when the tide went out. In a rock pool they found a small green crab. It waved one claw at them and then hid under a stone. Next to it a red starfish clung to the rock, holding on tight. Tess counted its five arms. Grandad said the pool was like a tiny town, busy with little animals, and that the sea would come back to cover it again by teatime.

title: The Library Cat
text: Every morning the library cat sat on the same sunny windowsill. Her name was Comma, because she always curled up in a little curve. Children read to her and she never once interrupted. One Tuesday a boy called Ravi read her a story about a lion. Comma listened to every word. When Ravi closed the book she stretched, yawned, and put one paw on the cover, as if she were asking for it again.

title: Moon Picnic
text: Nadia packed jam sandwiches, two apples and a flask of tea, because you should never visit the moon on an empty stomach. Her rocket was made from an old bathtub and a great deal of tape. It rattled all the way up, past the clouds, past the aeroplanes, past a very surprised seagull. On the moon everything was grey and quiet and covered in soft dust. Nadia laid out her blanket in a crater and poured the tea. It floated straight out of the cup in wobbling golden balls. She caught one in her mouth, which is the only sensible way to drink tea on the moon, and decided she would come back on Sunday.

questions.q: What was Nadia's rocket made from?

When did Nadia decide to come back?

title: The Winter Bus
text: The number nine bus broke down at the top of Hill Road on the coldest morning of the year. Everybody groaned. Mr Okafor, the driver, stood up and said that since they were all going to be late anyway, they might as well be late together. He opened his flask and shared it out in paper cups. A woman with a violin played three songs. Two boys cleared the snow from the windscreen without being asked. By the time the new bus arrived, forty minutes later, nobody on board could remember being cross. Mr Okafor said it was the best breakdown of his entire career, and he had had eleven.

questions.q: Where did the bus break down?
options: At the top of Hill Road

questions.q: What did the woman with the violin do?
How many breakdowns had Mr Okafor had?

text: Sid the snail wanted to win the garden race. "You are too slow!" laughed the ladybird. Sid smiled and kept going, one tiny inch at a time. title: The Night Market
text: Every Friday, the town had a night market. Lanterns hung above the stalls and glowed orange and gold. Ravi bought warm bread from the baker and a paper kite from an old man. A musician played a drum beside the fountain, and Ravi tapped his feet to the beat. On the way home, the kite danced behind him in the breeze.

title: The Brave Little Boat
text: A little red boat sat in the harbour and watched the big ships sail out to sea. "I am too small," she sighed. One foggy morning, a fishing crew got lost. The little boat had a bright lamp, so she shone it across the water. The crew followed the light and reached the shore safely. After that, everyone knew how brave she was.

title: The Bee Who Was Late
text: Bella the bee was always late for work. Each morning she stopped to watch the sunrise, and the other bees had already flown away. "Where were you?" asked the Queen. Bella showed her a field of purple flowers that she had spotted from the sky. The whole hive flew there and came home with sweet nectar. Now Bella is the first to know where the best flowers grow.

title: The Mountain Hut
text: Nina and her grandad climbed a steep mountain path. The air grew cold and the clouds came close. After three hours, they reached a small wooden hut. Inside there was a stove, two beds and a shelf of old books. Grandad lit a fire and made hot chocolate. Outside, snow began to fall softly. Nina pressed her nose to the window and watched the white flakes cover the trees. "This is the best day ever," she whispered. Grandad smiled and read her a story from one of the old books. They fell asleep to the sound of the wind.

title: The Clockmaker's Cat
text: In a tiny shop on Mill Street lived a clockmaker and his grey cat, Tick. The shop was full of ticking clocks, big and small. Every day at noon, Tick sat by the window and waited for the cuckoo clock to sing. One day the little bird stopped popping out. The clockmaker sighed, because his hands were too big to reach the tiny gears. Tick wriggled inside the clock and nudged a stuck cog with his paw. Cuckoo! The bird popped out, and the whole shop felt happy again. The clockmaker gave Tick a saucer of milk and called him the best helper in town.

title: The Lighthouse Night
text: Ana's aunt looked after the lighthouse on Seal Rock. Each evening, Ana helped her climb ninety-nine steps to switch on the great lamp. One night, a storm blew in and the power went out. Aunt Rosa found a box of candles and some mirrors. Together they lit a ring of candles, and the mirrors sent the glow far across the waves. A ferry that had lost its way turned towards the light and reached the harbour safely. In the morning, the captain brought them a basket of apples. "Thank you for keeping us safe," he said, and Ana grinned from ear to ear.

What did the captain bring?

title: The Desert Fox
text: Under the huge desert sky lived a small fox with enormous ears. Fennel slept all day in a cool burrow and came out when the sand turned chilly. One night, he heard a faint cry. A baby lizard was stuck under a heavy stone! Fennel pushed with his nose, then with his paws, until the stone rolled away. The lizard wriggled free and gave a happy flick of its tail. From then on, the lizards of the dunes always waved their tails when Fennel passed by. And Fennel always waved one big ear back at them, which made them all laugh.
